Capital Chronicle's view is that a dollar thesis needs this two-currency check before it is compared with Treasury yields.
The small moves in this five-date window show why a dollar view needs a named currency counterpart.
EURUSD is quoted in US dollars per euro.
When that number falls, one euro buys fewer dollars, so the dollar is stronger against the euro.
USDJPY is quoted in yen per dollar.
A fall means one dollar buys fewer yen, so the dollar is weaker against the yen.
The first chart puts both relationships into currency units per dollar and measures their change from October 26.
For the euro, that requires taking the reciprocal of EURUSD; the yen quote already measures what one dollar buys.

It reached 5.05% on October 28.
The endpoint fall was not a steady daily decline.
